segments.text: 800 ads for platforms, which campaigns had enough money and time, but still failed to earn back
their spend. Adlands turns the official mosaic data set into a traceable answer.
The complete source is preserved with a download timestamp and checks them.
Every ad retains its platform, audience, creative theme, spend, revenue, and running days.
Nothing is sampled out. An ad qualifies only when return on ad spend is below one.
Spend exceeds 5,000 rupees, and it has run for more than 14 days. All three must pass.
It's full spend counts once. The result, 14 lakh, 75,731 rupees, and 79 pace.
13 ads qualify. Instagram contributes the most, and the four platform totals reconcile exactly to
the answer. The Explorer makes that result practical. Filter by platform, audience, or creative
theme. Search for an individual ad, sort its performance, and open the evidence behind its
classification. Take this Instagram ad. It spent roughly one lakh, 39,000 rupees, and earned about
95,000. Its reported return is 0.68, over 65 days. All three checks pass, so its full spend
contributes once. The exact amounts and original source index remain visible. Creative rankings
use total revenue divided by total spend. Dr. Trust, lifestyle, and product demo lead.
These synthetic returns are unusually high, so relative under performance does not automatically mean
a whole audience is losing money. Python decimal and a separate JavaScript integer sense calculation
agree on every flagged ad and platform subtotal. Download the records and reconciliation to reproduce
the result. Adlands makes every rupee explainable. 13 ads, 14 lakh, 75,731 rupees, and 79 pace.
